items.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: We’ve got Sweets Edison playing one trumpet

ctx.x: Buddy Tate is not playing. But maybe it will come to me after. We’ve got Sweets Edison playing one trumpet, and we’ve got Al Grey playing trombone and oh, this is all changed up.
Yeah. You’ve got Junior Mance on piano?

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: it was Hank Jones, you can’t get any better on piano, Hank Jones, Milt Hinton, the Judge, Grady Tate, Buddy Tate, James Moody, Clark Terry, Al Gray and myself, Lionel Hampton.

ctx.x: Golden Men of Jazz, excuse me. Can you tell us a little bit about that group and working with it and where you’ve been with it and how it is getting together with some of these contemporaries so many years?

Well, I don’t know who had the idea, but it sure was a good idea. I don’t know whether it was Hamp or whether it his manager, Bill Titone, or who it was, but whoever it was, it was a good idea. Because when we opened up the first time in New York, it was Hank Jones, you can’t get any better on piano, Hank Jones, Milt Hinton, the Judge, Grady Tate, Buddy Tate, James Moody, Clark Terry, Al Gray and myself, Lionel Hampton. So, we’re all bandleaders in there, you know, and every place that we have gone, it’s been a…
As all being leaders and stars in your own right, were there any ego troubles on something like this?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And we went backstage at the Paramount where Lionel was with Benny Goodman.

ctx.x: It was common in those days, you know. And as you know, Mezz Mezzrow, he was the man around New York, you know. And at that time everybody went by the apartment house where he used to live, 2040, you know, and it was just automatic that you'd knock on the door for a couple of joints, you know.

I met him when I first came here. And we went backstage at the Paramount where Lionel was with Benny Goodman. And Mezz used to have a 50 flat tin of Chesterfield cigarettes in his right pocket and then he had another tin, the same type, in this pocket, which was not Chesterfields.

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And I’m going to the Kennedy Center on the 8th to play a concert there for the President with Lionel Hampton.

ctx.x: Tell us about what you’re doing today.

For the future? Well I’m not going on the road no three hundred one-nighters anymore that’s for sure. I’m through with that. But I have, I’m going to Chicago in the morning to play a festival with Clark Terry. And the 13th I’ll be at the Hollywood Bowl, the last jazz series of the summer, a tribute to Lionel Hampton which is called “Vibes.” And I’m going to the Kennedy Center on the 8th to play a concert there for the President with Lionel Hampton. And I’m going to Europe, going to Paris at a place called the…
